title: The Silver Leaf Band and sheet music
summary: Silver Leaf read sheet music under Albert Batiste then Oscar Randall, with little ragtime.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I was going to ask some more about the Silverleaf Band. What kind of music they played? Did they play ragtime or was it more blues? Did they use sheet music all the time?

They used sheet music. Yeah, well I'll tell you. See, Albert Baptiste, he led the Silverleaf Band when I first started for a while. And then he was a coffee potter. He worked for O'Keeffe on Magazine Street. That case. Yeah. And it kind of helped with his job. So then he turned over to Oscar Randall. I guess you remember him.

Randall. He was a pretty good violin player. And so he took up several of his bands and Albert's players for a while because the band began to draw a little bit and waking up, he couldn't get out to sheet. And so he had to let somebody else play. So Oscar Randall, he took it then. And we played sheet music. Wasn't much on the ragtime. Did you ever play anything by ear at all?
